jarOnlyRows.statement: Rules strings that hold a lone surrogate (an escape such as '\uD83D') load and evaluate by UTF-16 units in both profiles, as the official emulator does (owner 2270 (2), completed by 2276): length, +, ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=, contains, beginsWith, endsWith, replace (an empty target between the halves of a pair included), toLowerCase, toUpperCase and matches. A path or key that holds one names nothing: child() reads absent, hasChild and hasChildren are false and an index is undefined, so the negated forms read as the official emulator reads them. Production has not answered these shapes, so they are unobserved in production and the strict profile follows the jar. A string a rule builds past 2^26 UTF-16 units is an error here (the official emulator answers 500 from a heap-dependent size); that bound is a difference, not a lone-surrogate one. Case conversion is measured before it allocates, in both paths. A single rule evaluation that does more than 2^28 units of work (MAX_EVALUATION_WORK: one unit for each UTF-16 unit a string operation reads, copies or converts, so a quadratic `contains` or repeated concatenation stops) is an error here, which the official emulator answers from the memory and time of the machine; the most any one evaluation of the recorded Rules corpora does is 43 units, and a test holds every corpus under 2^18. What stays different (not claimed): a token whose claims hold a lone surrogate, and a query value that holds one (see knownDifferences.loneSurrogateClaimsAndQueryValues).

jarOnlyQueryOrderBy.statement: query.orderBy loads in both profiles and decides as the official emulator does (owner 2276; production documents it): it is the child ordering when the read orders by a child, otherwise a value that equals only itself, so `query.orderBy == null` is false and `query.orderBy != null` is true on a plain read, a stream and a listen, and null in a write, a validation and a shallow read. Rules that use it were refused at load before, so none was in force; the rules that can now allow a read are those that name query.orderBy. Unobserved in production, so strict follows the jar.

jarOnlyRegexEscapesAndUnits.statement: Emulator profile only (owner 2276): a pattern is read by UTF-16 unit as the official emulator reads it (a character beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane is two class members, and `.` takes one unit, so '😀' does not match /^[😀]$/ nor /^.$/ and matches /^..$/; a class range ends at the high surrogate of an astral end); after a backslash CR, CR LF, U+2028 and U+2029 are a line feed, and U+FEFF and U+0085 are themselves (U+00AD, U+200B and the other format characters are dropped with the reader, as before). The strict profile keeps today's refusal. Unobserved in production.

jarOnlyRegexDialect.statement: Emulator profile only (owner 2276): in a regular expression `\W` and `\D` are the complement of a language of strings (`'ab'` and `''` match `/^\W$/`, `'a'` does not), a class that holds one is the union of its members as languages, a negated class is single characters, an escaped letter or digit other than d, w, D and W is that character (so `/[\uD800-\uDFFF]/` is the class of `0` to `u`, `D` and `F`), a quantifier at the start of an alternative is that character, and a class is read by the official emulator's grammar (a range whose end is before its start holds nothing, `[\\a]` holds `a`, a `-` before the closing bracket is a character, `(?` is a group followed by a literal `?`). The strict profile keeps today's refusal (the rule is an error, so false negated or not) because production has not answered these shapes. 252 of the 323 corpus rows that fireemu denied and the official emulator allowed now decide as it does, and no corpus row moves the wrong way. 71 stay denied, which the emulator profile therefore still refuses where the official emulator admits: every one uses the `i` flag with non-ASCII text, which needs a Java 21 case-folding table (a declared difference, owner ledger line 2288; see knownDifferences.regexIFlagNonAsciiEmulatorProfile). A pattern is read by UTF-16 unit (a character beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane is two class members and two units for `.`), and after a backslash CR, CR LF, U+2028 and U+2029 are a line feed and U+FEFF and U+0085 are themselves, as the official emulator reads them (289 jar rows, jarOnlyRegexEscapesAndUnits).

jarOnlyBodyLoneSurrogate.statement: Emulator profile only (owners 2276 and 2286): a lone surrogate escape in a string value is stored as `?`, one for each lone surrogate and a valid pair untouched, as the official emulator stores it, in a REST write body (PUT, PATCH, POST; an object, an array, `.value` and `.priority` included), in a WebSocket frame (put, merge, `.priority`), and in an import file (the PUT /.json that firebase-tools sends); a bound of a REST query or a WebSocket listen (`startAt`, `endAt`, `equalTo`, `sp`, `ep`) reads `?` the same way. A key that holds one stays refused on both profiles, a WebSocket path that holds one is `invalid_parameters` "Invalid token in path" as the official emulator answers it, and so is a merge entry with any invalid key. The strict profile refuses all of them as before, an import file while the import is prepared, before any section is installed (the preparation takes one value saying how the Realtime Database values parse, set from the profile); production has not answered them. The surrogate is read from the text of a body or frame; the stored form of `?` is the official emulator's own (Java replaces a lone surrogate when it encodes the string).

jarOnlyClaimsAndQueryValues.statement: Emulator profile only (owner 2286): the claims of a token keep a lone surrogate (`"x":"\ud83d"`, a claim name and `sub`/`uid` included), as the official emulator holds them as Java strings: `auth.token.x == '\uD83D'` holds and its length is 1. The claims stay ordinary strings (a lone surrogate reads `?`, so every other reader, event payload and echo sees the ordinary value); the places that held a lone surrogate travel in a separate typed table (`LoneClaims`, crates/fireemu-core-database/src/lone.rs) that only the RTDB Rules binding reads, and the binding turns it into an evaluation-local view that is never stored or shown (a valid string that resembles the earlier encoding is just that string). The `authvar` of a frame is detected from the parsed frame, not from its text. A query value that holds one reads as `?` (query.startAt == '?' holds, == '\uD83D' does not). The daemon reads the claims from a copy of an unsigned token (empty signature) only; the signature of a signed token is always verified against its original payload, so a signed token whose payload holds a lone surrogate is not read (401) and no normalised substitute is ever verified. The strict profile does not read such a token (401) and refuses such a query value with 400 as before. Unobserved in production. 76 jar rows.

longPollingIdleClose.statement: A long-polling client that goes offline without closing has its onDisconnect writes run when the server drops the idle connection: production after 99.3 s to 104.0 s in the four recorded flows (100.8 s and 104.0 s in the onDisconnect recording, 99.3 s and 103.2 s in production-5), fireemu after 104.3 s to about 105 s (100 s idle timeout plus the client's poll timing). The event sequence is identical; the comparison judges the delay within 5 s of production's range.

cv11WriteAfterDeleteRace.statement: After user A is deleted, the admin write's acknowledgement and the listener's value event race in both production and fireemu; the comparison judges the events of that step (and only that step) unordered; every other step, including the multi-event steps signin-a, signout, resignin-a and refresh-after-delete, is judged in recorded order. Transport request counts (long-polling HTTP requests per profile) and millisecond timings are not compared.

sseFraming.statement: Production sends close-delimited event streams and closes after the cancel event. Under strict, fireemu closes after cancellation but uses native HTTP/1.1 chunked framing; the recorded event bytes agree. The emulator profile retains its existing transport behavior. The owner accepted this transfer-framing difference on 2026-10-31 (scope decision R8); this does not relax event, cancellation or EOF checks or establish whole-parent parity.

googleSignedTokens.statement: Local RTDB accepts only ID tokens issued by fireemu's Auth (or the owner credential); production Google-signed tokens are not accepted locally, and strict refuses a non-owner gauth credential with production's permission_denied.

triggerEventShapeEmulatorProfile.statement: The emulator profile delivers an RTDB trigger event in the official emulator's shape, not production's: a UUID event id instead of the base64 of twenty bytes, the full-precision time (nine fraction digits) instead of three, the session's project instead of `_` in a 2nd gen `source`, `datacontenttype: application/json`, and authType admin or unauthenticated (with the matching 2nd gen `context.authType`) where production says unknown; it sends no `traceparent`. The strict profile matches production in all 72 rows. Compared on 28 deliveries of the 8 handlers over 9 writes (recorded 2026-10-27, CV14-RTDB-TRIGGERS-20261027-02). The same holds for the 69 rows of the trigger breadth recording (RTDB-TRIGGERS-BREADTH-20261105-02), where the emulator profile also names a user's write authType admin or unauthenticated instead of app_user and USER. In the breadth rows the first-generation context also lists its member keys differently (extras.context.keys).

rootWriteListenOrder.statement: Official-emulator-only difference with no production answer: a write that covers several of a connection's per-path listens below it (recorded as an onDisconnect value at /k fired when the writer disconnects, with the observer listening at /k/s, /k/t, /k/u, /k/v and /k/s/n and not at /k) reaches the observer in depth order on fireemu (s, t, u, v, s/n) and in path-text order on the official emulator 4.11.2 (s, s/n, t, u, v). Production was not observed for this shape; it is registered as a known difference and not changed.

bodyKey768Bytes.statement: Official-emulator-only difference with no production answer: a key of 768 bytes in a write's JSON body is accepted by fireemu and refused with 400 by the official emulator 4.11.2 (which accepts the same key in the URL path, as fireemu does). Production documents keys of up to 768 bytes but was not observed for this shape; the emulator profile refuses less than the official emulator here, and the difference is registered as a known difference and not changed.

restEmulatorFollowsOfficialEmulator.statement: In 3 of the 72 REST cases the emulator profile answers as the official emulator (jar 4.11.2) and not as production: writeSizeLimit with a word or a number (the jar's text lists the limits in its own order, production in another) and a malformed % escape in the path (the jar answers 400 JSON Bad Request with CORS, production 400 octet-stream Bad request. 33 bytes without CORS or cache headers). The strict profile answers all 72 as production. In the print=silent DELETE the emulator profile answers as production (no content-length), where the jar answers 0.

invalidCredentialsEmulatorProfile.statement: The emulator profile follows the official emulator for invalid credentials, which production refuses: an alg:none token, any non-empty Bearer token and any access_token are accepted (11 of the 27 cases), and so is an RS256 or HS256-shaped token with a signature fireemu cannot verify in the recorded shape (own project as aud, a tenant that exists if it names one, exp in the future, a non-empty signature; unsigned tokens admitted and no session signer installed). The emulator profile refuses forged signed tokens outside that shape, which the official emulator admits and production refuses (listed in refusalsOutsideTheRecordedShape): this extends to RTDB the exception of owner decision 713 (Firestore and Storage), as an intentional declared difference (owner 2270 (1)). The huge token (about 4.8 KB, otherwise the same shape as the RS256 one) is accepted as well. The jar answers 400 to it because the request line exceeds a limit of about 4 KB (a token of 4054 characters passes, 4064 does not); that is a transport limit, not a decision about the credential: the same token passes as a Bearer and over WebSocket. Production answers 401, a refusal that belongs to the strict profile. fireemu has no request-line limit, and a size cap on the token would add a refusal the jar does not make, so none is applied. The strict profile answers all 27 cases as production.

loneSurrogateClaimsQueryValuesFramesEmul.statement: Official-emulator-only difference with no production answer: on the emulator profile a token claim that holds a lone surrogate is read, a lone surrogate in a query value, a WebSocket frame value or an import file value is `?`, as the official emulator does; the strict profile does not read such a token and refuses such values as before. Found by the pin of the Opus delta review S3 and fixed by owner 2286. Found with it and fixed on the emulator profile (the strict profile is unchanged): a WebSocket frame is read once and its path is validated in that read, so a frame whose path holds a lone surrogate answers `invalid_parameters` and writes nothing; a WebSocket merge entry whose key is not a valid path is answered `invalid_parameters` ("Invalid token in path", "Empty strings are not valid keys" for the empty key, the path length and depth texts) where the connection error was sent and the empty key was accepted; the `authvar` of a `gauth` frame keeps a lone surrogate and is echoed as the object in the answer (it was read with `?` and the answer said null). The echo lists the members in the order of the map, not in the order sent.
